output.summary: Found three setup defects using isolated, fake-only probes. Checkout unchanged. Standard tests were blocked by incompatible Zod and missing MCP dependencies; check/typecheck were blocked by missing Biome and Bun types. Isolated probes stubbed unrelated eval/review validators.

findings.title: Apply changed config to an already-running daemon
findings.detail: The service step only checks the preflight daemon status. If init writes new providers or a merge policy while the daemon is healthy, it skips installation/restart. Factory loads these settings at startup, so setup reports success while the daemon retains its old configuration. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" reload` printed providers.added=[claude,codex,local-1234], effects=[smoke,mcp], then failed: `AssertionError: new provider config must reach the already-running daemon`.
findings.suggestion: When effective runtime settings change, safely reload or restart the service and wait for readiness. Preserve the no-restart behavior when nothing changes.
findings.failure_scenario: A healthy daemon is running when init detects a new local provider or adds github.merge="pr". Config is written, but subsequent runs still use the previous catalog or merge default.

findings.title: Check requested repository access before writing config
findings.detail: Doctor runs before repositories supplied through --repo or prompts are considered, and only reads a repository already in config. Fresh setup therefore never verifies access or organization SSO for its requested repository. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" repo`, with a fake repository API returning an SSO 403, printed `{"code":0,"ghReads":[],"effects":["smoke","mcp"]}` and failed: `AssertionError: init must reject a requested repository with denied SSO access`.
findings.suggestion: Collect requested repositories and perform their access checks before any config or service mutation, preserving the SSO fix text and failure behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: On an empty config, run init --yes --repo private-org/denied with gh authenticated but lacking organization SSO authorization. Setup writes config and proceeds without detecting the access failure.

findings.title: Run smoke checks against the effective provider catalog
findings.detail: The production smoke adapter calls the existing smoke main, which uses hard-coded PROVIDERS/MODELS rather than the config catalog. Newly detected local providers and custom endpoints are never exercised; both native CLIs are always exercised even when doctor permits one to be missing. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" smoke` enumerated checks with a zero budget and no network. It reported detected=[claude,codex,local-1234], but smoke names contained only built-in providers, then failed: `AssertionError: smoke must exercise the detected local provider`.
findings.suggestion: Build setup smoke checks from the newly loaded effective catalog and available CLI providers, passing configured endpoints, models, and credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: Init detects a server on port 1234 and saves local-1234, but smoke never invokes it. Alternatively, a machine with only Claude passes preflight with a Codex warning and then fails smoke by invoking the absent Codex CLI.

Output: AssertionError: executed command substitution must be detected; false !== true.
findings.suggestion: Inspect executable substitutions inside double quotes while preserving the distinction between executable shell syntax and literal or escaped text. Add parser coverage for this case.

findings.title: Do not reject ordinary media based on incidental byte sequences
findings.detail: clean() rejects any occurrence of short signatures such as MZ anywhere in media bytes, including legitimate PCM samples. The new parser also rejects ordinary PNG text metadata. Changing those PCM samples leaves a valid WAV.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unrequested content validator and apply the specified inert-media path policy. Any future content-validation policy should be separately scoped and avoid treating arbitrary sample bytes as executable content.

findings.title: Process-group cleanup still lets detached descendants survive
findings.detail: The new exit handler kills and polls only the invocation's original process group. A descendant started with detached:true (or setsid) belongs to another group and survives after runProcess resolves, violating the required whole-tree cleanup. Reproduction command: bun --eval 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e",`const c=require("child_process").spawn("sleep",["3"],{detached:true,stdio:"ignore"});c.unref();console.log(c.pid)`],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env}); const pid=Number(r.stdout.trim()); console.log("descendant alive after return:",process.kill(pid,0)); process.kill(pid,"SIGKILL");' Output: descendant alive after return: true. This existing limitation remains unresolved by the requested fix.
findings.suggestion: Track invocation descendants across process-group changes and terminate them before returning. Add coverage for a detached background writer on normal completion and cancellation.

round recovery recognizes error: false
Command failed (1): git clean -fdq
warning: could not remove untracked`.

findings.title: Working directory and birth time do not prove process ownership
findings.detail:
The orphan fallback claims unrelated processes merely because they started during the invocation and share its working directory. On this macOS host, the following command demonstrated that finishing runProcess killed a separately launched control process:

bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts";const p=runProcess({cmd:["/bin/sleep","0.5"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env});await Bun.sleep(100);const c=Bun.spawn(["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 5 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $!"],{cwd:process.cwd(),env:{PATH:"/usr/bin:/bin"},stdout:"pipe"});const pid=Number(await new Response(c.stdout).text());await c.exited;try{console.log("alive before",process.kill(pid,0));await p;try{console.log("alive after",process.kill(pid,0))}catch(e){console.log("alive after",e.code)}}finally{try{process.kill(pid,"SIGKILL")}catch{}}'

Output:
alive before true
alive after ESRCH
findings.suggestion: Require demonstrated invocation ownership before signaling a process. Remove the cwd-based ownership inference and use retained ancestry or another reliable containment mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: Another worker or the user starts a background platform tool in the same directory during an invocation. When that invocation finishes, Limitless kills the unrelated process.

findings.title: Detached children with replaced environments survive shutdown
findings.detail:
An unmarked detached orphan with a visible, nonempty replacement environment is excluded from the hidden-process fallback. runProcess therefore reports successful shutdown while its child remains alive. Reproduced with:

bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts";const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e",`const c=require("child_process").spawn(process.execPath,["-e","setTimeout(()=>{},5000)"],{detached:true,stdio:"ignore",env:{FOO:"bar"}});c.unref();console.log(c.pid)`],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env});const pid=Number(r.stdout);try{console.log("background alive after return",process.kill(pid,0))}finally{process.kill(pid,"SIGKILL")}'

Output:
background alive after return true

The Linux implementation also relies on inherited markers and has no ancestry fallback.
findings.suggestion: Track descendants independently of their inherited environment, including detached descendants, and add coverage for a child launched with a replacement environment.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer's launcher supplies a clean environment to a detached background writer and exits. Shutdown misses the writer, allowing it to race with worktree cleanup—the original failure remains possible.

output.summary: Two direct subprocess checks exposed unsafe process ownership and surviving background writers. Targeted suites could not load because installed dependencies are missing or incompatible; bun run check stopped because biome is unavailable. The flagged repos.ts contains no NUL bytes. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Do not infer process ownership from working directory and birth time
findings.detail: The orphan fallback claims unrelated processes merely because they started during the invocation and share its working directory. Cleanup then signals those processes. A direct reproduction launched an independent orphan from the reviewer process while runProcess was active. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts". Output: {"invocationExit":0,"unrelatedPid":34184,"unrelatedAlive":false}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must survive invocation cleanup'.
findings.suggestion: Require evidence of invocation ancestry or an invocation-specific ownership boundary before signalling a process. Add coverage for an unrelated orphan born during the invocation in the same directory.
findings.failure_scenario: Another task or user starts a detached process in the same checkout while an invocation runs; its launcher exits. Invocation cleanup kills that unrelated process.

findings.title: Detached descendants can still outlive invocation cleanup
findings.detail: Discovery loses descendants that detach, replace their environment, and change directory outside the invocation roots before their parent exits. runProcess then reports successful termination while the child continues writing into the worktree by absolute path. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-escape.ts". Output: {"invocationExit":0,"descendantPid":39246,"descendantAlive":true}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: invocation descendant must be stopped before runProcess returns'. This leaves the original cleanup race possible and violates the whole-process-tree requirement.
findings.suggestion: Track descendant ownership throughout the invocation, or use an OS ownership boundary that survives environment replacement, detachment, and directory changes. Confirm those descendants have stopped before returning.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached background shell with a clean environment and an external working directory. The shell writes to an absolute worktree path, and the implementer exits. Cleanup proceeds while the writer remains alive.

output.summary: Found two process-ownership failures using direct subprocess checks on macOS. The binary audit flag was not reproduced: repos.ts contains no NUL bytes. Targeted tests could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing; bun run check stopped because biome is unavailable.

findings.title: Do not infer process ownership from an orphan's working directory
findings.detail:
An unrelated orphan born during an invocation is classified as its descendant when it shares the working directory. Shutdown consequently signals processes belonging to other invocations or the user. Reproduced with this exact command:
bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {spawnSync} from "node:child_process"; let sibling; try { const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e","console.log(\"ready\"); setTimeout(()=>{},300)"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env,onStdoutLine:()=>{const s=spawnSync(process.execPath,["-e","const c=require(\"node:child_process\").spawn(\"/bin/sleep\",[\"30\"],{env:{},detached:true,stdio:\"ignore\"}); console.log(c.pid); c.unref()"],{encoding:"utf8"}); sibling=Number(s.stdout.trim()); console.log("unrelated sibling",sibling); }}); console.log("invocation",r.exitCode); let alive=true; try{process.kill(sibling,0)}catch{alive=false} console.log("unrelated sibling alive:",alive); if(!alive) process.exitCode=1; }finally{if(sibling)try{process.kill(sibling,"SIGKILL")}catch{}}'
Output (exit 1):
unrelated sibling 32729
invocation 0
unrelated sibling alive: false
findings.suggestion: Require proven invocation ownership before signalling a process. Working directory and birth time cannot establish ancestry; use tracked ancestry or an OS containment mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, an independent launcher starts a detached process with an empty environment in the same checkout and exits. Finishing the invocation kills that unrelated process.

findings.title: Actual descendants can still outlive successful invocation shutdown
findings.detail:
The acknowledged fallback limitation leaves the requested whole-tree shutdown incomplete: a detached descendant with a replaced environment and a different cwd survives, while runProcess returns success and permits cleanup. Reproduced with this exact command:
bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; let pid; try {const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e","const c=require(\"node:child_process\").spawn(\"/bin/sleep\",[\"30\"],{cwd:\"/\",env:{},detached:true,stdio:\"ignore\"}); console.log(c.pid); c.unref()"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env}); pid=Number(r.stdout.trim()); let alive=true; try{process.kill(pid,0)}catch{alive=false} console.log("invocation exit:",r.exitCode,"descendant alive:",alive); if(alive)process.exitCode=1;} finally{if(pid)try{process.kill(pid,"SIGKILL")}catch{}}'
Output (exit 1):
invocation exit: 0 descendant alive: true
This escape also existed with the previous process-group implementation, but the requested fix still does not cover it.
findings.suggestion: Track descendants independently of inherited environment and cwd, and add coverage for a detached child that replaces its environment and changes directory.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached writer with env:{} and cwd outside the checkout, writing into the checkout through an absolute path. The implementer exits; shutdown reports success while the writer continues racing cleanup.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long-running commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This bridge buffers command output and sends its JSON response only after executeReaderCommand finishes, so commands taking longer than that can lose their HTTP connection despite the much larger configured command and MCP timeouts. The request signal also participates in command cancellation, so the disconnect can terminate verification.
findings.suggestion: Set idleTimeout: 0 on the invocation-owned server and retain the existing subprocess timeout and cancellation controls. Add a bridge regression test with a command lasting longer than 10 seconds.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier calls the command tool with `sleep 15; echo passed` and timeoutMs/idleTimeoutMs of 180000. The HTTP connection times out before the successful command result can return.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, surrounding confinement code, tests, and CI changes. Found a timeout defect in the new command bridge. Targeted tests could not load because the MCP SDK is missing; bun run check stopped because Biome is missing. Local socket and Seatbelt checks were denied by this session's sandbox.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for verification commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This endpoint buffers its JSON response until executeReaderCommand finishes, so commands lasting longer than 10 seconds lose their HTTP connection regardless of the configured subprocess and MCP tool timeouts. The request abort signal also feeds into subprocess cancellation. Ordinary verification suites can therefore still fail as environment-blocked.
findings.suggestion: Disable the server idle timeout, or disable it for command requests using server.timeout(req, 0), while retaining subprocess timeouts and cancellation. Add coverage for a command that takes longer than the default HTTP idle timeout.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier calls the reader command tool with a test suite that takes 20 seconds. No HTTP response data is sent during execution, so Bun closes the connection after approximately 10 seconds and the verifier receives a transport failure instead of the test result.

findings.title: Do not substitute an entire criterion from one embedded test command
findings.detail: The matcher extracts a Bun command from arbitrary instructions and ignores additional verification steps. A passing unit test therefore turns a blocked application HTTP check into met, allowing normalizeVerify to approve unverified behavior. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {applyGateEvidence as apply} from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; const sha="a".repeat(40), result={command:"bun test",ok:true,exitCode:0,output:"a.test.ts:\n(pass) unit"}; const v=apply({criteria:[{id:"A",status:"blocked"}]},{acceptance_criteria:[{id:"A",how_to_verify:"Run `bun test a.test.ts` then start the app and check HTTP 200"}]},{scenarios:[]},sha,{sha,checks:[{verdict:"pass",result,testCommand:"bun test"}]}); console.log(v.criteria[0].status); if(v.criteria[0].status!=="blocked") throw Error("Unchecked HTTP behavior was marked met");' Output: met, followed by error: Unchecked HTTP behavior was marked met (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Require the complete verification instruction to describe only the covered command, or use structured coverage requirements. Leave composite criteria blocked when gates do not cover every step.
findings.failure_scenario: A criterion requires running a unit test and starting the application to check HTTP behavior. Gates pass the unit test, but the verifier cannot start the application because loopback listening is denied. The factory incorrectly marks the entire criterion met.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and verification flow. Confirmed a false-pass defect with a targeted regression test. Repository tests could not load because installed Zod lacks overwrite(); bun run check stopped because Biome is unavailable.

findings.title: Require gate evidence to cover the entire criterion
findings.detail: The regex extracts a Bun command from longer verification instructions and ignores the remaining steps. A passing test therefore converts an entire blocked criterion to met even when an additional manual check remains unverified. Targeted command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.test.ts". Output: Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"; 0 pass, 1 fail.
findings.suggestion: Restrict substitution to instructions consisting entirely of a supported test command, or track and resolve individual verification steps without overriding unresolved steps.
findings.failure_scenario: A holdout says: "Run `bun test test/loopback.test.ts`. Then start the CLI with a temporary database and verify that an outbound connection is denied." Gates pass the loopback test, but the verifier reports blocked because the manual check encounters EPERM. applyGateEvidence marks the whole holdout met, allowing delivery without verifying outbound denial.

output.summary: Found two reproducible verification regressions. With a temporary preload selecting the available Zod v4, 111 focused tests passed and two additional regression checks failed. findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the loopback fallback
findings.detail: The clean-result predicate rejects any skipped file, and applyGateEvidence requires every gate to satisfy it. Limitless deliberately skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its successful suite cannot attest to a fully passing loopback test in another file. The reported verification block therefore remains for this repository. Reproduction command: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-gate-repro.test.ts". Output: '(fail) unrelated skipped file', 'Expected: "met"', 'Received: "blocked"'. The temporary preload selects the installed Zod v4.
findings.suggestion: Validate skipped-test coverage against the requested files. Allow an unrelated skipped file when retained coverage proves that every test in the requested file passed.
findings.failure_scenario: Confined bun test passes test/loopback.test.ts but skips a nested Seatbelt test in test/sandbox.test.ts. The reader cannot bind loopback, and the engine rejects the otherwise valid gate evidence, leaving verification blocked.

findings.title: Independent evidence mentioning a gate is discarded
findings.detail: gateClaim matches any standalone occurrence of 'gate', even when the verifier describes independently observed behavior. Sanitization then changes a met criterion to blocked and deletes its evidence. Reproduction command: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-gate-repro.test.ts". Output: '(fail) independent evidence mentioning gate', 'Expected: "met"', 'Received: "blocked"'. The evidence was 'bun test test/loopback.test.ts: 1 pass, 0 fail. This directly exercises the gate profile.'
findings.suggestion: Restrict sanitization to claims that rely on factory gate results or supplied provenance; preserve independently observed evidence that merely discusses gate behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier successfully runs a targeted test and reports that it exercises the gate profile. With no substitutable gate record, the engine converts the successful observation into an environment block and can terminate the run as needs_human.

output.summary: Found two verification regressions using isolated helper checks. Targeted tests could not load because installed Zod lacks existing required APIs; `bun run check` stopped because Biome is missing.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable all gate-evidence substitution
findings.detail: A skipped test anywhere invalidates the entire gate run, even when the requested file passed completely. This repository intentionally skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal successful suite cannot unblock loopback verification. An isolated `bun run -` check using passedFiles=['test/loopback.test.ts'] printed `clean suite: met`; adding skippedFiles=['test/sandbox.test.ts'] printed `unrelated skipped Seatbelt tests: blocked`.
findings.suggestion: Evaluate skipped coverage against the requested tests. Preserve rejection when the requested coverage is incomplete without rejecting unrelated intentional skips.
findings.failure_scenario: The confined full-suite gate passes the loopback test and skips nested Seatbelt tests. The reader cannot bind loopback, and verification still ends as environment-blocked despite successful coverage of the requested test.

findings.title: Ordinary mentions of gates invalidate independent verification
findings.detail: The sanitizer treats any standalone 'gate' mention as a factory citation, and checks global notes for every criterion. Consequently, notes such as 'Independently tested gate timeout handling.' downgrade every met criterion to blocked, including rows containing independently observed passing commands. The isolated `bun run -` check returned status `blocked` while retaining evidence `bun test test/loopback.test.ts: 1 pass, 0 fail`.
findings.suggestion: Restrict sanitization to actual provenance claims and affected rows. Do not invalidate independently observed evidence based on general vocabulary in global notes.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier successfully tests gate-related functionality and mentions that functionality in its notes. Criteria requiring inspection or commands unavailable in gate records become blocked and can terminate the run as needs_human.

output.summary: Inspected the diff and reproduced a defect that leaves normal confined verification blocked. Targeted test files could not start because installed Zod lacks the existing schema's overwrite API.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable gate evidence in normal factory runs
findings.detail: Every gate must pass the global skipped-test check before coverage is considered. This repository intentionally skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates (test/confinement.ts), so its normal full-suite gate cannot attest to even a completely passing loopback test. The reader profile remains unchanged, leaving the reported verification failure unresolved. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {applyGateEvidence as apply} from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; const sha="a".repeat(40), command="bun test"; const result=apply({criteria:[{id:"AC-1",status:"blocked",blockedReason:"sandbox"}]},{acceptance_criteria:[{id:"AC-1",how_to_verify:"bun test test/loopback.test.ts"}]},{scenarios:[]},sha,{stageId:1,sha,checks:[{verdict:"pass",blocking:false,testCommand:command,result:{ok:true,exitCode:0,command,output:"",testCoverage:{passedFiles:["test/loopback.test.ts"],skippedFiles:["test/sandbox.test.ts"]}}}]}); console.log(result.criteria[0]); if(result.criteria[0].status!=="met") throw Error("Expected passing loopback coverage to satisfy AC-1");'. Output: status "blocked", evidence "Factory gate substitution unavailable: candidate gate checks did not all pass cleanly without retries or skipped tests.", followed by "error: Expected passing loopback coverage to satisfy AC-1" (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Evaluate skipped coverage against the required tests, allowing unrelated intentional skips while continuing to reject skipped required tests. Add a regression covering a passing loopback file alongside skipped Seatbelt tests.

findings.title: Unrelated platform skips disable loopback gate evidence
findings.detail: The global skipped-test rejection prevents substitution even when retained coverage proves the required loopback file passed. findings.failure_scenario: The factory runs this repository's configured bun test gate under LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1. The loopback test passes, real Seatbelt tests skip as designed, and the verifier reports its loopback sandbox block. Substitution is refused and the run still ends needs_human.

findings.title: Allow unrelated skipped files when the requested test passed
findings.detail: The global skippedFiles check rejects evidence even when the requested file passed without skips. This repository's full-suite gate intentionally skips Seatbelt tests inside confinement, so the reported loopback verification failure remains unresolved with its normal gate configuration. Targeted reproduction command: bun -e 'import { applyGateEvidence } from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const sha="a".repeat(40); const result={ok:true,exitCode:0,output:"",testCoverage:{passedFiles:["test/loopback.test.ts"],skippedFiles:["test/sandbox.test.ts"],summary:{passed:1,failed:0}}}; const actual=applyGateEvidence({criteria:[{id:"AC-1",status:"blocked",blockedReason:"sandbox",evidence:"EPERM"}]},{acceptance_criteria:[{id:"AC-1",criterion:"tests pass",how_to_verify:"bun test test/loopback.test.ts"}]},{scenarios:[]},sha,{sha,stageId:12,checks:[{verdict:"pass",blocking:false,testCommand:"bun test",result}]}); assert.equal(actual.criteria[0].status,"met",actual.criteria[0].evidence);' Output: AssertionError: Factory gate substitution unavailable: candidate gate checks did not all pass cleanly without retries or skipped tests. 'blocked' !== 'met'.
findings.suggestion: Check skipped coverage against the requested files. Preserve rejection for skips in requested files or whole-suite verification, while allowing unrelated platform skips. Add a regression using the repository's normal full-suite gate configuration.

output.summary: Found two authentication compatibility regressions. Seven delivery tests passed; all 11 timed-out land-script cases passed with a longer timeout. Land-queue and retry checks were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies. No files were modified.

findings.title: Preserve trusted helpers selected by remote-URL conditions
findings.detail: Replacing the common config removes remote URLs needed by trusted global includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url conditions. A network-free probe with a global conditional credential.helper returned credentials before isolation, but invoking the same credential lookup through the wrapper produced "fatal: could not read Username for 'https://example.invalid': terminal prompts disabled" and exit 128. Thus existing global authentication settings can stop working on every push path.
findings.suggestion: Make the trusted destination available to conditional global includes in the isolated config, without copying untrusted repository settings, and add a regression test for a hasconfig-selected helper.
findings.failure_scenario: The global config conditionally includes a credential helper for repositories whose remote URL matches https://example.invalid/**. The checkout matches, but the isolated push config contains no remote URL, so authentication fails.

findings.title: Preserve the trusted transport for SSH-authenticated installations
findings.detail: The manual land push now always uses HTTPS. An installation that previously pushed through an SSH origin using SSH keys or a global core.sshCommand now needs separate HTTPS credentials. Preserving core.sshCommand in the wrapper does not help because HTTPS never invokes SSH. This violates the requirement to retain existing SSH authentication.
findings.suggestion: Select an explicit destination using trusted factory or global transport configuration, preserving SSH support without consulting the checkout's remote settings.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner uses git@github.com:MattFlower/limitless.git with working SSH authentication and has no HTTPS credential helper or global URL rewrite. The previously successful manual land push now fails authentication.

output.summary: Found a reproducible trusted-credential regression. Seven delivery tests and both modified land-pr push tests passed with a longer timeout. Other checks encountered timeouts or missing dependencies: biome, Bun types, and the MCP SDK.

findings.title: Preserve trusted URL-conditional credential configuration
findings.detail: Replacing GIT_COMMON_DIR removes remote URLs used by trusted global includeIf "hasconfig:remote.*.url:…" conditions. Consequently, credential helpers and SSH settings supplied by those global includes disappear during the push, breaking existing authentication. The HTTP-free probe `python3 "$TMPDIR/push-conditional-review.py"` printed `Before wrapper: credential fill succeeded`, then `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://example.invalid': terminal prompts disabled`, followed by `AssertionError: trusted global URL-conditional credentials lost during push`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve applicable trusted global/system conditional configuration while excluding repository configuration. Add a regression test with a global hasconfig conditional include supplying credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's global config conditionally includes their credential helper based on remote.origin.url. Normal credential lookup succeeds, but every factory push through this wrapper loses that helper and cannot authenticate.

output.summary: Reviewed all push paths and ran network-free probes. Repository config still executes commands in delivery and land-queue pushes. Delivery tests passed; manual-script tests had 18 timeouts, with five selected cases passing under a longer timeout. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Protect the delivery and land-queue pushes too
findings.detail: Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch excludes repository config or overrides command-running settings. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push.ts"` against a local bare remote with a repository-scoped URL rewrite and protocol.ext.allow=always produced `delivery: marker=true` and `land: marker=true`; both remote SHAs still matched the pinned SHA. These two explicitly required push paths remain vulnerable.
findings.suggestion: Apply shared push hardening to both functions: exclude repository config, preserve trusted global/system settings, and force protocol.ext.allow=never.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants a URL rewrite to an ext helper that creates a marker and forwards to the local Git transport. Subsequent delivery or land-queue publication executes that helper.

findings.title: Exclude untrusted config during the actual push
findings.detail: The final push still uses origin and reads live repository config. Validation and snapshot comparison only inspect earlier state; they do not prevent a background process started by unconfined PR checks from planting remote.origin.receivepack after the last snapshot. The actual push also lacks the required protocol.ext.allow=never override.
findings.suggestion: Push to the trusted explicit URL with repository config excluded, retaining safe_git hardening and the pinned SHA.
findings.failure_scenario: A background child of bun run check updates repository config after config_after is captured but before git push reads it. The push then executes the planted receivepack command.

findings.title: Do not reject harmless repository settings
findings.detail: The new allowlist blocks ordinary repository-local identity settings, preventing landing before checks even start. Invoking validate_repository_config in a temporary repository with a valid origin and local user.name/user.email returned exit 1 and printed `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land` and the equivalent user.email error. The request requires ignoring untrusted push settings, not banning unrelated repository configuration.
findings.suggestion: Isolate config for the push instead of imposing a repository-wide key allowlist.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator configures their commit identity locally rather than globally and runs land-pr.sh on an otherwise valid checkout.

findings.title: Allow sufficient time for the expanded subprocess tests
findings.detail: `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts` finished with `45 pass`, `18 fail`, and `14 errors`; all 18 failed cases exceeded the default 5000ms timeout, causing subsequent assertion failures. Running `bun test --timeout 30000 test/land-pr.test.ts -t 'tampering: redirect$'` passed in 8130ms. The four receivepack/SSH/helper/include cases also passed with the longer timeout, taking 6.7–8.1 seconds each.
findings.suggestion: Set an explicit timeout appropriate for these subprocess-heavy cases, as the delivery tests already do, or reduce their subprocess overhead.
findings.failure_scenario: The normal test command runs these expanded cases on a slower or loaded macOS machine and terminates them before validation or publication completes.

output.summary: Confirmed command execution through all three push paths using local-only probes. The new allowlist also rejects harmless repository settings. bash syntax validation passed. Landing tests finished with 49 passes and 14 five-second timeouts; an isolated redirect test passed with a 30-second timeout.

findings.title: Apply config isolation to delivery and land-queue pushes
findings.detail: Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch was changed. Both still consume repository-scoped URL rewrites and command settings through worktreeGit. A local probe using repository-scoped url.<ext-command>.pushInsteadOf and protocol.ext.allow=always executed a marker-writing command in both paths. Command: bun run "$TMPDIR/review-push-config.ts". Output: "delivery: marker=true, exactSHA=true" and "land: marker=true, exactSHA=true". These are unresolved security requirements of this change.
findings.suggestion: Use shared push isolation for both functions: exclude repository config, retain trusted global/system settings, and explicitly disable the ext protocol.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants a repository-scoped pushInsteadOf rewrite to an ext transport. Delivery or the land queue pushes the pinned SHA and executes the planted command.

findings.title: Exclude repository config instead of checking it before use
findings.detail: The final snapshot does not isolate the subsequent push: safe_git still reads live repository config and pushes to origin. A child left running by unconfined checks can modify config after the comparison. A probe using the exact added functions, then planting remote.origin.receivepack between the final comparison and push, executed the command. Command: bash "$TMPDIR/review-manual-config.sh". Output: "manual: marker=true after final validation" and "manual: exactSHA=true".
findings.suggestion: Push to the trusted explicit URL with repository config excluded and protocol.ext.allow=never, preserving the existing hardening and SHA pin.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR-spawned background process installs receivepack after config_after is read but before git push reads the config.

findings.title: Allow harmless local configuration without blocking landing
findings.detail: The allowlist rejects every unlisted local key before installation or checks, including ordinary user.name, user.email, core.autocrlf, and additional remotes. The request requires ignoring repository config for pushes, rather than making such repositories impossible to land. The local probe command bash "$TMPDIR/review-manual-config.sh" produced "Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land" and "local identity rejected".
findings.suggestion: Confine config isolation to the push operation so harmless checkout settings do not prevent landing. Test that planted command settings are ignored while the pinned SHA is successfully pushed.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner sets git config user.name in a normal checkout and runs land-pr.sh; the script now exits before running checks.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and both parser paths. A direct detector check reproduced premature loop detection when the sixth result changes. The harness tests could not load because the installed Zod lacks .overwrite().

findings.title: Wait for the threshold call's result before declaring a loop
findings.detail: observe() returns the stop reason before the current call's result arrives. Both harnesses immediately abort on that reason, so observeResult() cannot rescue a changed sixth result. Reproduced with: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i=0;i<6;i++) { const reason=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i),i<5?"waiting":"progress"); if(i===5 && reason) throw new Error(reason); }'. Output: error: repeated the same shell call 6 times. The added tests change results before reaching this boundary and miss the defect.
findings.suggestion: Defer the repetition verdict until the threshold call's result can be compared, while preserving budget enforcement and handling results that never arrive. Add regression coverage where the first five outputs match and the sixth differs.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent polls a test log five times with unchanged output; the sixth poll would report newly completed tests. Both harnesses abort at the sixth tool_call before receiving that progress.

findings.title: Wait for the threshold call’s result before committing to a loop stop
findings.detail: observe() returns the stop reason before the current call’s result arrives. Both harnesses immediately abort and permanently set stuckReason, so observeResult() cannot rescue a sixth call whose output changes. Reproduced with command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { assert.equal(d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)), null); d.observeResult(String(i), "waiting"); } const reason = d.observe("shell", "poll", "5"); d.observeResult("5", "1 test passed"); assert.equal(reason, null, "a changed sixth result must not stop a progressing poll");'. Output: AssertionError: a changed sixth result must not stop a progressing poll; actual: 'repeated the same shell call 6 times'; expected: null.
findings.suggestion: Make repetition decisions account for the threshold call’s result before irreversibly aborting, while preserving counting for missing results and the unchanged tool budget. Add a regression with five identical results followed by a changed sixth result through both harnesses.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polling calls return 'waiting'. The sixth poll returns '1 test passed', but its tool_call event has already triggered cancellation and marked the run stuck.

findings.title: Unresolved calls can be evicted without ever counting
findings.detail: Calls awaiting results remain uncounted until finish(), but eviction permanently discards them first. Consequently, six identical calls with missing results can escape detection entirely, violating the requirement that missing results retain today's counting. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const detector = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) detector.observe("shell", "poll", `missing-${i}`); for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) detector.observe("Read", { path: `file-${i}` }); const result = detector.finish(); console.log("finish:", result); assert.equal(result, "repeated the same shell call 6 times");' Output: finish: null; AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: actual null, expected 'repeated the same shell call 6 times'.
findings.suggestion: Account for unresolved calls before eviction can erase their repetition history, while preserving the ability for changed results to establish progress. Add a regression covering missing results followed by window eviction.
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation emits six identical shell calls whose results never arrive, then twelve distinct calls. No observation reports a loop, and finish() returns null, allowing the invocation to succeed despite the repeated unresolved calls.

findings.title: Unresolved calls no longer trigger live loop detection
findings.detail: Every unresolved call is excluded until finish(), and also blocks subsequent completions of its key. Repeated calls with missing results can therefore continue until the tool budget or timeout, contrary to the requirement that still-running calls retain today's counting. Reproduction: `bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); let r=null; for(let i=0;i<6;i++) r=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); console.log(r); if(r===null) throw Error("missing-result loop undetected");'` prints `null` and fails with `error: missing-result loop undetected`. Twenty unresolved identical calls likewise return no reason.
findings.suggestion: Preserve live counting for unresolved calls while allowing an arriving changed result to clear prior occurrences. Add a regression test that verifies detection during an active invocation with missing results, rather than only after finish().
findings.failure_scenario: An active agent emits six or more identical tool calls with distinct IDs and no results. Neither harness aborts at the existing repetition threshold; calls can continue until the separate budget or timeout.

findings.title: An unresolved sixth call no longer triggers loop detection
findings.detail: This condition suppresses detection until another tool call invokes reconcile(true) or the process exits and finish() runs. If the sixth identical call hangs without returning a result, neither happens while the invocation remains active. The agent consequently runs until an unrelated inactivity or invocation timeout, whereas the request explicitly preserves today's counting for still-running calls. A direct bun -e probe with five identical completed calls followed by one unresolved identical call returned null for all six observe() calls.
findings.suggestion: Ensure an unresolved threshold call can trigger detection while the invocation is still active, and add a harness test where the sixth call never completes and no seventh call occurs.

findings.title: Preserve the previous result hash after window eviction
findings.detail: Deleting the result baseline makes a changed result count as repetition when its preceding call has left the window. Reproduction: `bun -e 'import {LoopDetector as D} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new D(100); d.observe("shell","poll","a"); d.observeResult("a","old"); for(let i=0;i<12;i++) d.observe("Read",i); for(let i=0;i<6;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i),"new");} console.log(d.finish());'` outputs `repeated the same shell call 6 times`; expected `null`, because the first new result is progress and only five subsequent calls repeat it.
findings.suggestion: Retain the previous result hash independently of window membership, and add a regression covering progress after eviction.

findings.title: Do not finalize pending results when another tool starts

Output: `AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: actual 'repeated the same shell call 6 times', expected null`.
findings.suggestion: Keep pending results eligible to establish progress while other tools start. Finalize missing results at invocation completion and retain the existing tool-call budget.

Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/smoke-review.test.ts"` used fake harnesses and a zero execution budget to inspect scheduled checks; it listed only built-in provider rows and failed `Expected: true; Received: false` for inclusion of configured local-1234.

findings.title: Detect signals executed inside shell expansions
findings.detail: Double-quoted arguments are treated as opaque strings, and non-interpreter heredocs are discarded entirely. Both can execute command substitutions, so real kill attempts disappear from warnings, the feed, and reports. Targeted command: bun --eval 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("echo \"$(kill -TERM 123)\""), true);'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true.
findings.suggestion: Scan executable command substitutions in double quotes and unquoted heredocs while preserving literal handling for single quotes and quoted heredoc delimiters.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent submits echo "$(kill -TERM 123)" or an unquoted cat heredoc containing $(kill -TERM 123). The shell attempts the signal, but neither harness emits a warning.

findings.title: Preserve executable JavaScript template interpolations
findings.detail: jsSignal removes entire template literals, including executable ${...} expressions. A process.kill call inside an interpolation is therefore missed in both shell-invoked JavaScript and JavaScript tools. Targeted command: bun --eval 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("node -e '\''console.log(`${process.kill(123)}`)'\''"), true);'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish template text from interpolation expressions and inspect the expressions for process.kill calls.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent runs node -e 'console.log(`${process.kill(123)}`)'. JavaScript attempts the signal, but the event log and report contain no signal warning.

findings.title: Detect executable substitutions inside quoted shell arguments

Similar restrictions reject JPEG EXIF/comments and MP3 ID3 tags. This adds content restrictions absent from the request and blocks ordinary files in explicitly permitted formats. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501/review-inert-media.ts`. Both additions and edits output included `binary-content/block: author.png`; the otherwise identical PNG without the valid Author tEXt chunk passed.
findings.suggestion: Implement the requested media-path exemption without imposing this additional restrictive format validator.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid PNG containing a CRC-correct `Author\0Matt` tEXt chunk; the audit requires Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not remove media exemptions above 32 MiB
findings.detail: Any media blob larger than MEDIA_LIMIT is skipped and consequently included in binaryPaths, regardless of whether it is valid inert media. The request has no size-dependent allowance requirement. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501/review-inert-media.ts`. Both additions and edits output included `binary-content/block: silence.wav` for a valid mono PCM WAV with 32 MiB of samples plus its 44-byte header.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the requested path-based exemption regardless of blob size.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid WAV larger than 32 MiB without Allow: binary; the audit blocks it solely because of its size.

findings.title: Do not classify ordinary text by embedded signature substrings
findings.detail: isForbiddenFormat searches entire blobs for short signatures and ordinary strings, and repos.ts removes matching files from the text classification. Consequently, fully reviewable source and documentation require a binary allowance. This also explains the automated binary flags on this patch's text source files. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/audit-review.ts". Output: FAIL reviewable source is text actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"README.md"},{"rule":"binary-content","file":"country.ts"},{"rule":"binary-content","file":"format.ts"}] expected=[].

findings.title: Keep executable text scripts outside the binary allowance
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance unconditionally marks every changed 100755 file as binary, including existing shell scripts whose text is completely visible. It also marks removal of an executable bit when the blob is unchanged. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/audit-review.ts". Output: FAIL reviewable executable shell script is text actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"hello.sh"}] expected=[]; FAIL edit existing executable shell script is text actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"hello.sh"}] expected=[]; FAIL remove executable bit on shell script actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"hello.sh"}] expected=[].

findings.title: Final cleanup can mask the recoverable cleanup error
findings.detail: The gates callback always calls discardChanges in its finally block. When the two -ffdxq attempts leave an untracked, non-ignored directory that cannot be removed, discardChanges runs clean -fdq and throws CommandError. That replaces WorktreeCleanError, so this new handler rethrows and fails the run. Reproduced with the actual checkoutCommitted and discardChanges functions and a temporary Git shim that reports an untracked blocked directory and fails clean. Output: {"caught":"CommandError","roundFailureHandlerMatches":false,"message":"Command failed (1): git clean -fdq\nwarning: failed to remove blocked/file: Permission denied"}.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the original cleanup failure across the finally block, or classify failures from that final cleanup as round failures too when the implementer ended unsuccessfully.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer leaves a non-ignored directory whose contents cannot be removed. Both clean retries fail, then discardChanges fails on the same directory and bypasses round recovery.

findings.title: Process-group termination does not kill the whole descendant tree
findings.detail: The new exit handler still signals only the invocation's original process group. A descendant spawned with detached:true has another process group and survives. This is a pre-existing limitation left unresolved by the requested fix. Exact check: bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; const program = `const {spawn}=require("node:child_process"); const p=spawn(process.execPath,["-e","setInterval(()=>{},1000)"],{detached:true,stdio:"ignore"}); console.log(p.pid); p.unref();`; let pid; try { const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e",program],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env}); pid=Number(r.stdout.trim()); console.log(JSON.stringify({exitCode:r.exitCode,descendantPid:pid,aliveAfterReturn:process.kill(pid,0)})); } finally {if(pid)process.kill(pid,"SIGKILL");}' Output: {"exitCode":0,"descendantPid":15856,"aliveAfterReturn":true}. The check killed its own surviving child afterward.
findings.suggestion: Track or contain descendants across process-group changes and ensure they stop before returning control to worktree cleanup. Add coverage for a detached background writer.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached background writer with redirected stdio and then exits or is stopped. runProcess returns while the writer continues modifying the worktree during cleanup.

findings.title: Final cleanup can mask the recoverable cleanup error
findings.detail: After checkoutCommitted exhausts its clean retry and throws WorktreeCleanError, the gates' finally block calls discardChanges. If untracked files remain and that cleanup also fails, its CommandError replaces WorktreeCleanError. This handler rethrows it, failing the run instead of advancing the round. Reproduced with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-clean.ts"`: `checkout alone: WorktreeCleanError round handler catches: true` followed by `with gates finally: CommandError round handler catches: false`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the initial cleanup error through the finally block, or classify failures from both cleanup paths as recoverable after a failed implement round.

findings.title: Process-group termination still leaves detached descendants alive
findings.detail: killTree only signals the original process group. Descendants that create another session or process group survive, and the new wait returns immediately when the original group disappears. This leaves the requested whole-tree teardown incomplete. Reproduced with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-process.ts"`, spawning a Python child with start_new_session=True: output was `{"exitCode":0,"childStillAlive":true}`, followed by `error: Background descendant survived invocation completion`. This limitation predates the diff but remains an unmet requirement of this fix.
findings.suggestion: Track and terminate invocation-owned descendants across process groups, or use an invocation containment mechanism that reliably terminates all descendants. Add coverage for detached children.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent tool launches a detached background writer with redirected stdio. The agent exits normally or is stopped; runProcess resolves while the writer continues modifying the worktree during cleanup.

findings.title: Children with replacement environments survive shutdown
findings.detail: Processes with readable environments are selected only by invocation markers. A background Bun child spawned with env:{PATH:process.env.PATH,FOO:'bar'} loses those markers and is ignored even in the invocation's process group. The Linux scanner likewise requires markers. Standalone command `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-process-tree.ts` returned `{"exitCode":0,"childAliveAfterReturn":true}`. Cleanup can therefore begin while invocation descendants remain alive.
findings.suggestion: Retain process-group and ancestry tracking independently of environment markers, and confirm those descendants have stopped before returning.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a background writer using a sanitized environment and exits or stalls. The writer survives invocation shutdown and races worktree cleanup.

findings.title: Cwd and birth time incorrectly establish process ownership
findings.detail: Any hidden-environment orphan born after invocation start with a cwd under the worktree is treated as an invocation member, without evidence of ancestry. This kills unrelated processes sharing that directory. A standalone check launched an independent sibling launcher that orphaned a shell in the invocation cwd. Command `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-unrelated-orphan.ts` returned `{"exitCode":0,"unrelatedOrphanAliveAfterReturn":false}`.
findings.suggestion: Require observed ancestry, invocation markers, or another invocation-specific ownership mechanism before signaling an orphan. Do not infer ownership solely from cwd and birth time.

If this clean fails, it throws CommandError rather than WorktreeCleanError, so the new recovery handler rethrows it and fails the run. A standalone probe of this call's default behavior, `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-clean-retry.ts`, produced `{"errorType":"CommandError","cleanAttempts":1}` for a clean that would succeed on its second attempt.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same failed-implementer cleanup retry and error classification to the checkout before a gate timeout rerun.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer leaves partial work, gates time out only on the changed revision, and git clean fails once before the gate rerun. Even if final discard succeeds, the run fails instead of retrying cleanup or advancing rounds.

findings.title: Process discovery misses owned children with replacement environments
findings.detail: Session/group membership is accepted only when the environment is hidden. A regular executable launched with a replacement environment containing PATH but no invocation marker is excluded, even when it remains in the invocation's process group. Removing the previous group kill therefore introduces a regression: runProcess reports confirmed shutdown while the child keeps writing. The standalone same-group assertion failed with `Expected: 4; Received: 29` bytes after return; against the base implementation it passed with `sameGroupBytesAtReturn: 1, sameGroupBytesAfterReturn: 1`. The detached-shell case also failed (`Expected: 1278; Received: 9508`) when the shell changed cwd to / and wrote through an absolute worktree path.
findings.suggestion: Track invocation ownership independently of inherited environment and cwd, retaining safe termination of known process-group members and detached descendants before resolving runProcess.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a background test runner with an explicitly constructed environment, then exits or is stopped. The runner remains alive after runProcess returns and races with worktree cleanup.

findings.title: Cwd and birth time do not establish ownership of an orphan
findings.detail: The orphan fallback selects any hidden-environment process born after invocation start whose cwd is within a captured directory, without proving ancestry or marker ownership. An unrelated launcher can create exactly that state. The standalone native-inspection assertion printed `unrelatedOrphanSelected: true` and failed with `Expected to not contain: 81592; Received: [81592]`. stopMarkedProcesses will send SIGTERM and potentially SIGKILL to that selected process, allowing one invocation to terminate unrelated work.
findings.suggestion: Require positive invocation provenance before signaling an orphan. Do not use cwd and birth time alone as authorization to terminate a process.
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another launcher starts a detached macOS platform process in the same checkout or captured scratch directory and exits. Invocation cleanup selects and kills that unrelated orphan.

findings.title: Directory membership can cause teardown to kill unrelated processes
findings.detail: An unmarked orphan born after invocation startup is treated as owned solely because its cwd matches an invocation directory. This does not establish ancestry. An isolated fixture launched an independent shell from the reviewer process while runProcess was running; teardown killed that shell. Output: `{"mode":"unrelated","exitCode":0,"alive":false}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: independent unmarked process was killed`.

findings.title: Detached shells outside the captured directories still outlive invocation shutdown
findings.detail: Discovery happens during shutdown, after detached descendants can lose their parent chain. A macOS shell with a hidden environment and cwd outside the captured roots is then omitted, and shutdown returns success. This leaves the requested whole-tree guarantee unmet. Exact check: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501/review-process-membership.ts descendant`. Output: `{"mode":"descendant","exitCode":0,"alive":true}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: detached background child outlived invocation`. A separate check reproduced this with the invocation environment inherited.
findings.suggestion: Track descendant identity before reparenting, or use invocation containment that survives detachment and cwd changes. Do not confirm shutdown while such descendants remain unaccounted for.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long verification commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second connection idle timeout. This endpoint uses JSON responses and awaits the entire subprocess result before returning any bytes, so verification commands exceeding that interval lose their MCP connection even when the subprocess produces output. The request signal is included in the subprocess cancellation signal, so disconnecting can also terminate the test. Increasing the CLI tool timeout does not change this server timeout.
findings.suggestion: Set idleTimeout: 0 for this invocation-owned server, retaining the existing subprocess and invocation deadlines. Add a regression test that calls a reader command lasting longer than 10 seconds.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a test suite taking 20 seconds with timeoutMs set to 180000. The HTTP connection times out around 10 seconds before the command result is returned, causing a tool transport failure instead of successful verification.

findings.failure_scenario: A Rust repository uses a standard rustup installation with no explicit RUSTUP_HOME environment variable. Its cargo tests pass gates, but the verifier's reader command cannot discover the installed compiler after HOME changes to scratch, blocking verification.
