findings.failure_scenario: Instructions are `Run bun test loopback.test.ts, then manually verify outbound connections stay denied.` Gates pass loopback.test.ts, while the verifier reports the additional check blocked. The factory marks the whole criterion met without outbound-denial evidence.

findings.title: Require positive test execution evidence for targeted commands
findings.detail: The exact-file branch accepts a successful process whenever its output lacks failure or skip markers, even with no passing tests. Confirmed that Bun exits 0 and emits only its version and file header when a test module calls process.exit(0). Those actual output bytes are accepted as coverage. Targeted command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-AAmrsP/claude-501/review-gate-evidence.ts zero`. Output: `expected blocked; actual met`, followed by `error: Unverified criterion was marked met`.
findings.suggestion: Require captured passing coverage for every requested file, including exact targeted commands; missing execution evidence must leave verification blocked.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted loopback test exits successfully during initialization before registering or executing tests. Its gate passes with empty passedFiles, and a blocked verifier criterion is nevertheless converted to met.

output.summary: Found two ways gate evidence can incorrectly satisfy verification. A direct reproduction confirmed partial coverage becomes met. Targeted tests could not execute because installed Zod lacks .overwrite(); bun run check stopped because biome is unavailable.

findings.title: Do not treat one covered command as coverage of an entire scenario
findings.detail: The regex extracts a Bun command while ignoring additional instructions, then marks the entire blocked criterion met. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {applyGateEvidence as f} from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; const sha="a".repeat(40); console.log(f({criteria:[{id:"A",status:"blocked"}]},{acceptance_criteria:[{id:"A",how_to_verify:"bun test a.test.ts\nCheck outbound access is denied"}]},{scenarios:[]},sha,{sha,stageId:1,checks:[{verdict:"pass",blocking:false,testCommand:"bun test",result:{ok:true,exitCode:0,output:"a.test.ts:\n(pass) loopback"}}]}).criteria[0].status);' Output: met. No gate evidence covers the outbound check.
findings.suggestion: Restrict substitution to instructions entirely covered by the gate command, or track individual verification steps and retain blocked status for uncovered steps.
findings.failure_scenario: A scenario requests a loopback test followed by an independent outbound-denial check. Gates cover only the loopback test; the verifier reports blocked on the other step. The factory changes the whole scenario to met and can deliver without verifying outbound isolation.

findings.title: Check tested working-tree bytes before recording commit provenance
findings.detail: Evidence eligibility checks only HEAD, after discardChanges has erased gate modifications. Setup commands and earlier checks can modify tracked source or tests without changing HEAD. Subsequent tests then pass against those modified bytes, but the new evidence attributes that pass to the original commit and can override a blocked independent verification.
findings.suggestion: Detect tracked changes during gate execution and refuse commit-based substitution for checks affected by them. Perform this validation before discarding changes; checking HEAD alone does not establish which source bytes were tested.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured setup or fixing check rewrites a tracked source file so the loopback test passes. Gates succeed, discardChanges restores the broken committed file, and HEAD remains unchanged. When the reader cannot run the test, its blocked result becomes met using evidence from the repaired working tree.

output.summary: Found two reproducible verification regressions. With a temporary preload selecting locally available Zod v4, 111 existing focused tests passed; two adversarial assertions failed. Standard checks were blocked by missing Biome and incompatible installed Zod; pipeline integration tests were blocked by missing solid-js/web. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the loopback workaround
findings.detail:
passed() rejects any check containing a skipped file, and applyGateEvidence requires every check to satisfy passed(). Consequently, a successfully executed loopback test cannot supply evidence when an unrelated platform test is skipped. This repository deliberately skips tests when LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1, which runConfined sets, so its normal gates cannot supply the intended evidence. Reproduction: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod-preload.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.test.ts". The assertion 'an unrelated platform skip must not invalidate a passing loopback file' failed with:
Expected: "met"
Received: "blocked"
findings.suggestion: For targeted substitution, require complete passing coverage of the requested file without rejecting unrelated skipped files or checks. Retain stricter completeness requirements for whole-suite criteria.
findings.failure_scenario: The confined bun test gate exits zero and records test/loopback.test.ts in passedFiles, while a separate nested-Seatbelt test is skipped. The verifier cannot bind loopback, reports blocked, and the engine still ends verification as needs_human despite passing coverage of the requested test.

findings.title: Ordinary mentions of gates invalidate independent verification
findings.detail:
The sanitizer treats any standalone 'gate' as reliance on factory results, even in independently observed implementation evidence. It also applies a matching notes field to every criterion. Valid met results become blocked and their evidence is erased; inspection criteria cannot recover through command-based gate substitution. Reproduction: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod-preload.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.test.ts". The assertion 'independent code inspection mentioning a gate must remain met' failed with:
Expected: "met"
Received: "blocked"
findings.suggestion: Restrict sanitization to actual claims of relying on factory check results or supplied provenance. Preserve independent code observations and avoid invalidating unrelated criteria because of general notes.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier marks an authentication criterion met with evidence 'Inspected src/auth.ts:42: the authentication gate rejects a missing token before calling the handler.' The engine changes it to blocked despite no environmental failure, potentially exhausting verification retries and stopping delivery.

output.summary: Found three reproducible defects in gate evidence substitution. The 111 focused tests passed using a temporary bundle resolving Zod v4. Normal test execution was blocked by the available Zod version; bun run check stopped because Biome was missing. Repository files were unchanged.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable all gate evidence
findings.detail: passed() rejects any check containing skipped files, and applyGateEvidence requires every check to pass this predicate. Consequently, a passing loopback test cannot supply evidence when an unrelated test is skipped. This repository deliberately skips real Seatbelt tests under LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1, which runConfined always sets, so ordinary confined suite results retain the original verification blockage. Isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.js"` returned `unrelated skip: blocked` despite recorded passing coverage for test/loopback.test.ts.
findings.suggestion: Evaluate skips against the requested test coverage. Allow unrelated skipped files while requiring complete passing coverage of each requested file.
findings.failure_scenario: Confined bun test passes test/loopback.test.ts and skips test/sandbox.test.ts. The verifier cannot bind loopback and reports the loopback criterion blocked. The engine refuses substitution and ends verification as needs_human.

findings.title: A general note mentioning gates invalidates independent evidence
findings.detail: Every criterion is scanned against the entire verify.notes field. Any standalone mention of gates therefore converts every met criterion to blocked, even when the note explicitly disclaims reliance on gates and each criterion contains independently observed evidence. Isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.js"` returned `independent observation with notes: blocked` for notes saying 'I did not rely on gates; independently inspected the implementation.'
findings.suggestion: Avoid treating a general mention of gates as proof that every criterion depends on gate results. Preserve independently observed criterion evidence and restrict provenance validation to actual claims of reliance.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier independently validates all criteria, then mentions gates in its general notes. Criteria requiring inspection or commands unsupported by gate substitution become blocked and can terminate an otherwise successful run as needs_human.

findings.title: Exact command matching bypasses recorded file coverage
findings.detail: When requested and selected arguments match, covers() returns success without checking passedFiles. Bun treats bare test arguments as filename filters, so matching command strings do not prove the requested file ran. In a TMPDIR fixture containing only unrelated/test/loopback.test.ts, `bun test test/loopback.test.ts` exited successfully and printed `(pass) unrelated`. Feeding that result and its accurate coverage into the helper with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.js"` returned `wrong file ran: met` for the missing test/loopback.test.ts criterion.
findings.suggestion: Require recorded passing coverage for the requested files even when gate and verification commands match. Do not infer exact file execution from Bun filter arguments.
findings.failure_scenario: The criterion requires test/loopback.test.ts, but only unrelated/test/loopback.test.ts exists. The gate command matches and passes the unrelated file; the verifier reports an environment block. The engine incorrectly marks the required criterion met and attaches authoritative gate provenance.

output.summary: Found two reproducible defects in gate substitution. Direct resolver checks reproduced both. The targeted test suites could not load because the installed Zod lacks .overwrite(); no repository files were modified.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests prevent resolving the reported verification failure
findings.detail: Substitution requires every gate to contain zero skipped tests, even when coverage proves the requested file passed completely. This repository deliberately skips Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal full-suite gate cannot supply evidence for passing loopback tests. Since the reader profile remains unchanged, the original needs_human failure persists. Reproducer: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-383.ts" skips` outputs `expected met; actual blocked` and `AssertionError: 'blocked' !== 'met'`.
findings.suggestion: Evaluate skipped coverage for the requested tests rather than rejecting unrelated skipped files across the entire gate run. Add an integration case with a passing loopback test and an unrelated platform-specific skip.
findings.failure_scenario: The full-suite gate passes test/loopback.test.ts and skips test/seatbelt.test.ts as required inside confinement. The verifier reports a sandbox block for the loopback test. Substitution refuses the passing evidence and verification ends as needs_human.

findings.title: Targeted-command shortcut certifies a file that never ran
findings.detail: The shortcut normalizes away './' and accepts matching command arguments without consulting passedFiles. Bun treats an unprefixed argument as a substring filter, while './' selects a path. With only other-loopback.test.ts present, `bun test loopback.test.ts` passes but `bun test ./loopback.test.ts` fails with no matches. The resolver nevertheless marks the latter criterion met, even with coverage explicitly naming only the unrelated file. Reproducer: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-383.ts" filter` outputs `gate exit=0; requested command exit=1`, `expected blocked; actual met`, and `AssertionError: 'met' !== 'blocked'`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve Bun's path-versus-filter semantics and require recorded coverage of the requested file before substituting evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate runs the filter `bun test loopback.test.ts`, discovering only other-loopback.test.ts. A sandbox-blocked criterion requires `bun test ./loopback.test.ts`, whose file is absent. Verification incorrectly passes using the unrelated test.

output.summary: Found three defects in gate-evidence substitution, confirmed by targeted probes using real Bun execution where relevant. Repository files were unchanged. Existing targeted tests could not load because the installed Zod lacks .overwrite().

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the fix for confined factory gates
findings.detail: Any skipped test anywhere in the gate suite rejects substitution for every criterion, even when retained coverage proves the requested file passed completely. This repository deliberately skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal passing suite cannot resolve the reported loopback verification blocks. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/verifier-review.ucgpf7/repro.test.ts"` failed the passing-file/unrelated-skip assertion with `Expected: "met"; Received: "blocked"`.
findings.suggestion: Check skipped coverage for the requested files rather than rejecting the entire suite. Preserve rejection when required tests were skipped.
findings.failure_scenario: The full `bun test` gate passes a local-server CLI test and skips test/sandbox.test.ts cases because LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1. The verifier reports that CLI test blocked by its sandbox. Substitution refuses the passing evidence and the run still ends needs_human.

findings.title: Candidate-controlled output can fabricate authoritative test coverage
findings.detail: The collector treats arbitrary stdout/stderr as trusted runner headers and passing rows. A candidate test can print `test/loopback.test.ts:\n(pass) forged server check` and make the engine substitute a passing verdict for that nonexistent file. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/verifier-review.ucgpf7/repro.test.ts"` ran a real Bun decoy test, recorded `passedFiles: ["test/loopback.test.ts", "decoy.test.ts"]`, and failed with `Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"`.
findings.suggestion: Do not promote candidate-controlled console output into authoritative coverage. Use independently established execution provenance for the required command and fail closed when coverage cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A candidate contains only decoy.test.ts, which prints a fabricated passing header for the acceptance test. The broad gate exits successfully, and a sandbox-blocked acceptance criterion is marked met although its required test never existed or ran.

findings.title: Preserve Bun's distinction between substring filters and exact paths
findings.detail: Removing leading `./` makes different Bun commands equivalent, and the matching-command shortcut then accepts them without checking discovered files. Bun treats `test/loopback.test.ts` as a substring filter but `./test/loopback.test.ts` as an exact path. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/verifier-review.ucgpf7/repro.test.ts"` confirmed `substring exit 0 exact-path exit 1`, then failed substitution validation with `Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve argument semantics and require coverage of the actual requested path; remove the shortcut that assumes normalized matching arguments prove execution.
findings.failure_scenario: Only other/test/loopback.test.ts exists. The gate `bun test test/loopback.test.ts` passes that file, while the acceptance command `bun test ./test/loopback.test.ts` fails because its exact file is absent. The engine nevertheless marks the blocked acceptance command met.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and verification/resume paths. Direct probes reproduced false gate coverage and rejection caused by unrelated skips. Targeted tests could not load because installed Zod lacks number().overwrite; no repository files were modified.

findings.title: Test output can forge coverage for a file that never ran
findings.detail: The parser treats test-controlled console output as runner-generated file headers. A passing test that executes console.error("test/missing.test.ts:") causes its subsequent real passing row to be attributed to the nonexistent file. applyGateEvidence then marks a blocked criterion requiring that file as met. Reproduction command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501/review-gate-evidence.ts. Output: {"probe":"spoofed-header","missingExists":false,"actual":"met","expected":"blocked"}.
findings.suggestion: Obtain coverage through a channel that distinguishes runner records from test diagnostics, or run the required targeted command and validate its actual result instead of inferring coverage from console text.
findings.failure_scenario: An unrelated passing test prints the header of an absent or undiscovered required test. The verifier reports a sandbox block, and the engine substitutes fabricated coverage as authoritative factory evidence.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the fix for normal repository gates
findings.detail: Requiring every gate to pass without any skipped tests rejects evidence even when the requested loopback test passed completely. This repository's full-suite gate normally skips Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its successful results cannot resolve the reported verification block. Reproduction command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501/review-gate-evidence.ts. Output: {"probe":"unrelated-skip","actual":"blocked","expected":"met"}.
findings.suggestion: Reject skipped coverage for the required verification steps while allowing unrelated platform skips in otherwise successful gates. Add a regression covering a passing loopback test alongside a skipped Seatbelt test.
findings.failure_scenario: The full bun test gate passes the required local-server tests and skips an unrelated platform-specific test. Both verifier attempts encounter the reader's socket restriction; substitution refuses the successful gate evidence and the run still ends needs_human.

output.summary: Found two reproduced defects in gate-evidence substitution. Temporary fixtures exercised real `bun test` output and the new substitution functions. The requested targeted tests could not load because the installed Zod lacks `.overwrite()`: `bun test test/gate-evidence.test.ts test/verification.test.ts` reported 0 pass, 2 errors. No files were modified.

findings.title: Test-controlled output can forge authoritative file coverage
findings.detail: The parser treats arbitrary test stdout/stderr as runner-generated coverage. I ran `bun test` in a temporary directory containing only passing.test.ts, whose passing test printed `test/never-ran.test.ts:\n(pass) fabricated coverage`. The command exited 0 with `1 pass\n0 fail`; the parser recorded passedFiles=["test/never-ran.test.ts"], and applyGateEvidence changed the blocked criterion for that nonexistent file to `met` with factory provenance. This promotes output controlled by the change under test into authoritative verification evidence.
findings.suggestion: Do not derive authoritative file coverage from an undifferentiated test-output stream. Use independently established execution coverage, or retain the blocked status when coverage cannot be authenticated.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR adds console output resembling Bun file headers and passing rows to an unrelated passing test. Broad gates pass, and a sandbox-blocked verification of a file that never ran receives a successful factory citation.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable substitution for the actual target
findings.detail: Every gate must pass the global no-skips predicate before targeted coverage is considered. This repository intentionally skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates through LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1, so its normal broad `bun test` gate cannot supply evidence even when the requested loopback file passed completely. Reproduction: `bun test` in a temporary fixture with one passing target file and one unrelated skipped file exited 0; coverage showed the target in passedFiles and the unrelated file in skippedFiles. applyGateEvidence nevertheless returned `blocked` with `candidate gate checks did not all pass cleanly without retries or skipped tests`. The reader profile is unchanged, leaving the reported verification failure unresolved for this normal configuration.
findings.suggestion: For targeted verification, reject skips or incomplete execution affecting the required files rather than unrelated files elsewhere in the suite. Keep stricter completeness requirements for criteria requesting the entire suite.
findings.failure_scenario: A confined factory gate runs the full repository suite, passes the loopback tests, and intentionally skips unrelated Seatbelt tests. The verifier cannot bind loopback; both verification attempts remain blocked and the run ends needs_human despite usable gate results for the target.

output.summary: Found two reproduced compatibility regressions. Delivery tests passed; land-script timeout failures passed when rerun with a longer timeout. Land-queue tests could not load a missing SDK dependency. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Preserve trusted remote-conditional credential configuration
findings.detail: Replacing the common directory removes remote URLs used to evaluate trusted global `includeIf "hasconfig:remote.*.url:…"` blocks. Credential helpers and SSH settings in those blocks consequently disappear. An offline credential-fill probe succeeded before isolation with `username=test` and `password=trusted`, but running it through `bash scripts/push-git.sh <probe> push https://example.invalid/repo.git HEAD:refs/heads/main` returned 128: `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://example.invalid': terminal prompts disabled`. This violates the requirement to preserve existing global credential setup.
findings.suggestion: Resolve trusted system/global configuration, including conditional includes, in the original repository context and carry those trusted values into the isolated push configuration while excluding local/worktree entries.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's global config conditionally includes their credential helper based on remote.origin.url. Ordinary Git authenticates successfully, but factory delivery and land pushes lose the helper and fail authentication.

findings.title: Preserve reftable storage when constructing the isolated repository
findings.detail: The isolated repository copies only objects, refs and packed-refs, then declares repository format 0. It omits reftable storage and `extensions.refStorage`, so source references cannot resolve in a reftable repository. In a fixture created with `git init --ref-format=reftable`, `bash scripts/push-git.sh git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push --no-follow-tags "$url" HEAD:refs/heads/using-head` returned 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`; the same Git push without the wrapper succeeded. Normal delivery still calls pushBranch with `HEAD` in src/pipeline/engine.ts.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the source ref-storage format and its backing files, or resolve source references to exact object IDs before entering the isolated repository.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory repository uses reftable storage, for example through trusted global init.defaultRefFormat configuration. Normal delivery pushes HEAD through the wrapper and fails despite a valid commit and reachable local remote.

output.summary: Found three credential compatibility regressions. Delivery tests passed; land cases that timed out passed with a longer timeout. Land-queue tests could not load the missing MCP SDK dependency. Shell syntax and diff checks passed.

findings.title: Trusted URL-conditional credentials disappear
findings.detail: Replacing GIT_COMMON_DIR removes remote URLs used to evaluate trusted global includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url conditions. Consequently, credential helpers and SSH settings in those trusted includes disappear. A local probe with GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 confirmed that `git config --get credential.helper` returned `trusted-helper` before isolation, while `bash scripts/push-git.sh <capture> push https://example.invalid/repo.git HEAD:refs/heads/test` queried the same effective setting and returned exit 1 with empty output.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trusted conditional configuration using the factory's trusted destination, without restoring checkout-controlled command settings.
findings.failure_scenario: The global config selects a credential helper through a hasconfig remote-URL condition matching the checkout's origin. Ordinary pushes authenticate, but delivery and landing pushes lose that helper.

findings.title: The SSH default overrides trusted GIT_SSH
findings.detail: When core.sshCommand is unset, injecting core.sshCommand=ssh overrides Git's existing GIT_SSH environment setting. A network-free probe used GIT_SSH to run a local receive-pack: `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/before"` succeeded, while `bash scripts/push-git.sh git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/after"` exited 128 with `fatal: Could not read from remote repository.` The invocation markers were `trusted` followed by `fallback`, proving the wrapper bypassed GIT_SSH.
findings.suggestion: Honor trusted GIT_SSH when no trusted core.sshCommand is configured, preserving Git's SSH selection precedence.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation supplies its SSH identity or authentication wrapper through GIT_SSH and has no global core.sshCommand. Factory pushes now invoke plain ssh and fail authentication.

findings.title: Hardcoded HTTPS breaks existing SSH authentication
findings.detail: The final push previously used origin's transport and now always uses HTTPS. An SSH-only installation with working global SSH configuration gains no HTTPS credentials from that change, so landing fails after checks and the final scan. This violates the requirement to preserve existing helper or SSH authentication.
findings.suggestion: Obtain an explicit trusted remote URL from factory-owned metadata or GitHub's repository metadata while preserving the intended authentication transport.
findings.failure_scenario: The landing checkout has an SSH origin, authentication works through an SSH key, and no HTTPS credential helper or URL rewrite is configured. The final push switches to HTTPS and cannot authenticate.

output.summary: Confirmed two unresolved command-execution paths and a new compatibility regression using local, network-free probes. Delivery tests passed. Manual-script tests had two reproducible default-timeout failures; both passed with a longer timeout.

findings.title: Protect the delivery and land queue push paths
findings.detail: Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch receives the requested protection. Both still consume repository-scoped command settings through worktreeGit. A local probe invoking these exports with a planted core.sshCommand produced `delivery: repository command executed = true` and `land: repository command executed = true`. Command: `env -u GIT_SSH_COMMAND -u GIT_SSH bun "$TMPDIR/review-push-probe.ts"`. The planted command only created a marker and exited; no network was used.
findings.suggestion: Apply a shared push implementation that excludes repository config while preserving trusted global/system settings, existing hardening, and pinned refspecs.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants core.sshCommand in repository config. Delivery or land queue publication subsequently invokes that command.

findings.title: Config snapshots do not isolate the final push
findings.detail: The final push still reads repository config and targets origin. A surviving check subprocess can change config after the final snapshot. A local probe using the script's actual validation functions passed validation and snapshot equality, then planted core.sshCommand before the unchanged push invocation. Command: `bash "$TMPDIR/review-race-probe.sh"`; output: `After successful validation and equal snapshots: repository command executed = true`. The new checks leave the underlying vulnerability open.
findings.suggestion: Exclude repository config during the push itself and use an explicit trusted URL with protocol.ext.allow=never; do not rely on preflight snapshots.
findings.failure_scenario: An unconfined check leaves a background process that writes command-running config between the last snapshot and Git reading config for push.

findings.title: Allow ordinary repository configuration
findings.detail: The allowlist rejects harmless existing settings, including user.name, user.email, and additional remotes. This prevents otherwise valid repositories from landing. Command: `bash "$TMPDIR/review-config-probe.sh"`; a fresh repository passed, but adding only user.name produced `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land` and exit status 1.
findings.suggestion: Ignore repository settings for publication instead of requiring the entire repository configuration to contain only clone metadata.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer configures their commit identity locally and invokes land-pr.sh. The script exits before installing dependencies or running checks.

findings.title: Adjust the integration tests' execution budget
findings.detail: `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts` failed the missing and clean final-PR cases at 5000 ms. The isolated command `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'land validates the final PR after CI: (missing|clean)$'` reproduced both timeouts and `Expected: true, Received: false` at line 850. With `--timeout 30000`, both passed in 6406 ms and 6310 ms. The added config subprocesses leave these integration cases beyond their default timeout on this machine.
findings.suggestion: Give these real-subprocess integration cases an explicit suitable timeout or reduce their subprocess overhead.
findings.failure_scenario: The default check runs these cases on a loaded machine; Bun times them out and fails the suite despite their eventual successful behavior.

output.summary: Found two remaining command-execution vulnerabilities and a compatibility regression. Local probes reproduced all three without network access. Landing tests had 54 passes and nine default-timeout failures; all affected cases passed with a 30-second timeout.

findings.title: Delivery and land-queue pushes still execute repository-configured commands
findings.detail: The change only modifies the manual landing script. pushBranch and pushExistingBranch, which also serves the land queue, still read repository command and URL-rewrite settings without isolating trusted scopes or disabling ext transport. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push-probe.ts"` against local bare remotes printed `pushBranch: repository command executed = true ; exact SHA = true` and `pushExistingBranch: repository command executed = true ; exact SHA = true`. The probe planted a repository URL rewrite to an ext transport script and enabled that protocol locally. Both APIs executed the script.
findings.suggestion: Apply shared push-config isolation to both TypeScript push APIs, preserving trusted global/system credentials, existing hardening, and pinned refspecs. Explicitly disable ext transport.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants repository-level URL rewriting and protocol settings. Delivery or the land queue subsequently invokes a push using that repository, executing the planted transport command.

findings.title: The push still trusts repository config after its final snapshot
findings.detail: Validation and snapshot comparison do not isolate the subsequent push: it still targets `origin` and rereads mutable repository config. A process left running by the unconfined checks can install receivepack or pushurl after the snapshot. The local probe `python3 "$TMPDIR/review-config-probe.py"` used the script's actual functions and emulated that write between comparison and push. It printed `post-snapshot-write: exit 0` and `repository receivepack executed = True ; exact SHA = True`. Thus the pinned SHA does not prevent command execution in the protected window.
findings.suggestion: Push to the trusted explicit URL with repository config excluded from the push itself, retaining trusted global/system configuration and setting protocol.ext.allow=never.
findings.failure_scenario: A background process started during bun run check writes remote.origin.receivepack after config_after is captured but before git push reads the config.

findings.title: The allowlist blocks landing repositories with harmless local settings
findings.detail: The validator rejects every local key outside a narrow clone-metadata list, including ordinary user.name, user.email, and additional remotes. This changes normal landing behavior instead of excluding untrusted config only for the push. Running `python3 "$TMPDIR/review-config-probe.py"` with local user.name printed `local-identity: exit 1`, `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land`, and `Cannot validate repository git config; refusing to land`. The script stops before checks or publication even though this setting cannot execute a push command.
findings.suggestion: Isolate repository configuration for the push rather than rejecting unrelated repository settings. Add coverage that lands successfully with ordinary local identity settings and planted push-command settings.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer configures a repository-specific commit identity with git config user.name, then invokes land-pr.sh; landing immediately fails.

output.summary: Found two result-ordering defects using standalone detector checks. The targeted harness suite could not load because installed Zod lacks z.number().overwrite. No files modified.

findings.title: The sixth call aborts before its changed result can establish progress
findings.detail: observe() returns the stop reason before receiving the current result. Both harnesses immediately abort and retain stuckReason, so observeResult() cannot rescue the run. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<5;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult(String(i),"waiting");} console.log(d.observe("shell","poll","5"));d.observeResult("5","progress");' Output: repeated the same shell call 6 times. The changed sixth result should restart the count.
findings.suggestion: Defer the irreversible repetition verdict until the candidate result is known, while retaining budget enforcement and explicitly handling results that never arrive.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'; the sixth poll returns 'progress'. The harness aborts at the sixth call before considering its changed result.

findings.title: Late results overwrite the baseline of newer identical calls
findings.detail: results stores the last completion rather than the previous identical call in invocation order. An older completion can replace a newer hash, causing the next unchanged result to clear the window incorrectly. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100);for(let i=1;i<=3;i++)d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult("1","A");d.observeResult("3","B");d.observeResult("2","A");for(let i=4;i<=9;i++){const r=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult(String(i),"B");if(i===9)console.log(r);}' Output: null. Calls 4–9 repeat result B after call 3 established B, so the sixth repetition should stop.
findings.suggestion: Track result hashes by invocation order and reconcile adjacent identical calls when results arrive out of order; prevent older completions from replacing a newer baseline.
findings.failure_scenario: Identical calls 1–3 produce A, A, B but complete in order 1, 3, 2. Calls 4–9 all produce B. Call 4 is incorrectly classified as progress, delaying loop detection.

findings.title: Wait for the threshold call's result before declaring it identical
findings.detail: observe still returns a stop reason before the current result is available. Both harnesses immediately abort and retain stuckReason, so observeResult cannot rescue a progressing sixth call. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { const reason = d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i), i < 5 ? "waiting" : "progress"); assert.equal(reason, null, `call ${i + 1} must not stop when its result changes`); }'. Output: AssertionError: call 6 must not stop when its result changes; actual: 'repeated the same shell call 6 times'; expected: null.
findings.suggestion: Defer the irreversible repetition decision until the matching result is checked, while explicitly preserving counting for missing results and keeping budget enforcement immediate. Add a regression where the sixth result is the first changed result.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polling calls return 'waiting'; the sixth would return 'progress'. The harness aborts when the sixth call starts, before learning that it made progress.

findings.title: Compare results in call order rather than completion order

This makes a subsequent unchanged result look like progress and incorrectly clears the window. Output: AssertionError; actual: null; expected: 'repeated the same shell call 6 times'.
findings.suggestion: Track result hashes with call sequence numbers and reconcile each result against the preceding identical call, preventing stale completions from replacing the newer baseline.
findings.failure_scenario: Calls 1 and 2 return A, call 3 returns B, but completion order is 1, 3, 2. Calls 4 through 9 all return B. Call 4 is incorrectly treated as another change, so six unchanged calls fail to trip the detector.

findings.title: Missing results no longer count while the invocation runs
findings.detail: Calls awaiting results are excluded from counting, and an unresolved call also blocks later completions of its key. Six identical unresolved calls therefore never stop the active invocation. Subsequent calls can evict them before finish(), permanently losing the loop. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); let reason = null; for (let i=0; i<6; i++) reason=d.observe("shell", {command:"poll"}, String(i)); for (let i=0; i<12; i++) d.observe("Read", {path:i}, `read-${i}`); assert.equal(d.finish(), "repeated the same shell call 6 times");' Output: AssertionError, actual null, expected 'repeated the same shell call 6 times'. This violates the explicit requirement that still-running or missing results retain today's counting.
findings.suggestion: Preserve loop counting for unresolved calls while allowing received changed results to reset their key. Add coverage for missing results during an active invocation and across window eviction.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent emits six identical shell calls with distinct IDs and no results, then twelve unrelated calls. Neither the sixth repeated call nor invocation completion reports the loop.

findings.title: Missing results can suppress loop detection entirely
findings.detail: Unresolved calls remain uncounted until finish(), block later completions of the same key, and can be evicted before ever counting. This violates the requirement that calls whose results never arrive retain today's counting. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i=0;i<6;i++) console.log(`missing ${i+1}:`, d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i))); for (let i=0;i<12;i++) d.observe("Read", {path:String(i)}, `read-${i}`); console.log("finish:", d.finish());'. Output: missing 1: null through missing 6: null, then finish: null. The previous detector stops at the sixth shell call. A separate direct check also showed that one unresolved call suppresses detection across seven subsequent completed calls with identical results.
findings.suggestion: Preserve counting for unresolved calls without letting a missing result indefinitely block completed repetitions or disappear uncounted on eviction. Add regression coverage for unresolved calls followed by completed repetitions and window eviction.
findings.failure_scenario: Six identical tool calls receive no results, then unrelated calls evict them from the window. The invocation ends without a loop verdict. Alternatively, an early unresolved call blocks later identical completed results until it leaves the window.

findings.title: Out-of-order results can stop calls whose outputs all differ
findings.detail: Only the last call's unresolved result delays detection. If six parallel identical calls complete in reverse order, the sixth call's result immediately triggers a stop before the preceding results can establish progress. Both harnesses abort on that verdict. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as a } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<6;i++) d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)); a.equal(d.observeResult("5", "5"), null);' Output: AssertionError: actual 'repeated the same shell call 6 times', expected null. Feeding equivalent real-shaped Claude events reproduces the same failure.
findings.suggestion: Account for unresolved predecessors when deciding whether a completed threshold call repeats its previous result. Add coverage where six different results arrive in reverse order, while preserving counting for results that never arrive.
findings.failure_scenario: Six identical calls are issued concurrently, with respective outputs 0 through 5. Call 5 completes first; the detector returns stuck immediately and the harness cancels the invocation before the remaining distinct results arrive.

findings.title: Do not finalize pending results when another tool starts
findings.detail: Every observe() calls reconcile(true), treating a pending threshold result as finished merely because another tool starts. Both harnesses then abort immediately, so a changed result cannot establish progress. The new 'pending threshold result' test explicitly expects this incorrect cutoff. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; import {strictEqual} from "node:assert"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<5;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",`${i}`);d.observeResult(`${i}`,"waiting");} d.observe("shell","poll","sixth"); strictEqual(d.observe("Read","file","other"),null); d.observeResult("sixth","progress");' Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: actual 'repeated the same shell call 6 times', expected null.
findings.suggestion: Keep pending results eligible to establish progress across overlapping calls. Reconcile them when their results arrive or the invocation finishes, while preserving the tool-call budget. Replace the test that requires stopping on the next call with coverage for overlapping calls whose results change.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'. A sixth poll starts and will return 'progress', but an unrelated Read starts before that result arrives. The detector reports a loop and both harnesses cancel the progressing invocation.

findings.title: Do not finalize pending results when another tool call starts
findings.detail: `observe()` calls `reconcile(true)` before registering every new call. Consequently, starting a seventh call treats six pending calls as a confirmed loop, although their eventual results may all differ. Both harnesses immediately abort on that reason. Reproduced with: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); const reasons = []; for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) reasons.push(d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i))); for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) reasons.push(d.observeResult(String(i), `progress ${i}`)); console.log(JSON.stringify(reasons)); assert.equal(reasons.find(Boolean), undefined, "seven parallel calls with different results must not be classified as a loop");' Output: [null,null,null,null,null,null,"repeated the same shell call 6 times",null,null,null,null,null,null,null], followed by AssertionError.
findings.suggestion: Keep pending calls eligible for result comparison across subsequent tool starts; finalize unresolved calls at invocation completion. Add coverage for more than six parallel calls with changing results.

findings.title: An unrelated call prematurely finalizes pending results

findings.title: Window eviction forgets the previous identical call's result
findings.detail: Deleting results when a key leaves the window prevents comparison with the previous identical call, as required. After a gap, a changed result incorrectly counts as the first repetition. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); d.observe("shell","poll","old"); d.observeResult("old","waiting"); for(let i=0;i<12;i++){d.observe("Read",i,"r"+i);d.observeResult("r"+i,"file");} for(let i=0;i<6;i++){console.log("call",i,d.observe("shell","poll","p"+i));console.log("result",i,d.observeResult("p"+i,"progress"));}' Output ends with "result 5 repeated the same shell call 6 times"; all earlier calls/results print null. The first 'progress' result differs from 'waiting' and should not count, leaving only five repetitions.
findings.suggestion: Retain the last result hash independently of window membership, while continuing to bound repetition counting to the existing window. Add a test with a changed result after the previous identical call has been evicted.
